claim_verdicts.evidence: general.md: MediaQuery.sizeOf and LayoutBuilder are two valid ways, "depending on whether you want the size of the whole app window, or more local sizing"; MediaQuery.sizeOf returns "the size of the app window in logical pixels". So a window-size check already sees a narrow browser window correctly; only the side-panel case needs LayoutBuilder. "keeps working" as a blanket rule is not in the docs.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Deciding from the size of the whole app window gives the wrong answer when this widget gets only part of that window, such as a panel beside another panel. Its constraints describe the space this widget actually has, wherever it is placed.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, false by execution. Center gives SizedBox loose constraints capped at the test view (800x600 logical by default), so SizedBox(width: 900) is clamped to 800. Probe test on stage-1 copy: `requested=900.0 viewLogical=Size(800.0, 600.0) layoutBuilderSize=Size(800.0, 400.0) gridColumns=2`. LayoutBuilder gets 800, not 900; the grid has 2 columns, not 3. Docs (constraints.md): "The Center tells the Container that it can be any size it wants, but not bigger than the screen."
issues.quote: so the constraints `LayoutBuilder` receives are 360 or 900 pixels wide, whatever the test screen's own size is
issues.fix: Replace with: "`catalogWithWidth` places the catalog inside a box of the given width, but a box can never be wider than the space its own parent allows. The test screen is 800 pixels wide by default, so at 360 the catalog gets 360, and at 900 it gets 800: still wide enough for a grid (2 columns)." Add a claim for this to .meta.json (source: flutter test probe). Or ask for a repo change (prompt 08) to set the test view size.

issues.text: Explanations for q5 (correct and option b) repeat the false statement that the catalog decides from 900 whatever the test screen's size. At 900 the SizedBox is clamped to the 800-pixel test view (see section 5 blocker). The key `a` is only fully true for 360.
issues.quote: so the catalog decides from 360 or 900 whatever the test screen's own size is
issues.fix: Change option a to "So `LayoutBuilder` gets a limited width, up to the size the screen allows" and the correct explanation (en/vi) to: "The box limits the room its child gets: 360 in the narrow test. It cannot exceed the test screen, so the 900 box is clamped to 800, still wide enough for the grid." In b's explanation, drop "or 900".

issues.text: Columns are not 300 pixels wide. crossAxisCount = floor(maxWidth/300) and SliverGridDelegateWithFixedCrossAxisCount splits the full width evenly, so each column is maxWidth/columns (750 → 2 columns of 375; 800 → 2 of 400). 300 is the minimum column width, not the column width. Also "above" misses 600 itself, which gets the grid (code: `< 600` → list). Section 5 "how many 300-pixel columns fit" is acceptable; the summary is not.
issues.fix: Line 3: "`ProductCatalog` returns a one-column `ListView` below 600 pixels, and from 600 up a `GridView` with as many columns as 300 pixels fits into the width."

issues.text: In Flutter the usual whole-screen check, MediaQuery.sizeOf, returns the size of the app window (general.md: "return the size of the app window in logical pixels"). In a 500-pixel browser window it reports ~500, not the monitor width, so "a narrow browser window" is not a case where it breaks. Only the side-panel case is. The Situation ("wider than 1920") and the Try-it answer ("A check on the monitor's width would see a very wide screen") present a monitor-width check as the realistic alternative.
issues.quote: breaks as soon as the widget sits somewhere else: a narrow browser window on a big monitor, a panel beside another panel, a tablet turned sideways
issues.fix: Section 4: use claim 6 suggested_text and keep only the panel example. Section 7 extra question: set the catalog in a 500-pixel panel beside an order form in a wide window (as quiz q4 does), not a 500-pixel browser window. Answer: a check on the window's width sees a wide window and picks the grid; LayoutBuilder sees 500 and picks the list.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and wrong as a Flutter behaviour. A widget with a fixed width larger than its parent's maximum is clamped, not overflowed (constraints.md: a widget "can't have any size it wants"; probe: SizedBox(width: 900) laid out at 800). A ListView gives its rows tight cross-axis constraints, so a 400-pixel row on a 360-pixel phone is laid out at 360. Overflow happens in a Row whose fixed children add up to more than the width.
issues.quote: a list with fixed 400-pixel rows overflows a 360-pixel phone and leaves most of a monitor empty
issues.fix: Replace with: "You notice this when a row laid out for exactly 400 pixels gets squeezed or cut off on a 360-pixel phone and leaves most of a monitor empty." Or drop the overflow wording. Add a claim to .meta.json if a specific behaviour is kept.

issues.text: Unlisted claim about the layout protocol (min/max width and height from parent). It is true (constraints.md: "A widget gets its own constraints from its parent. A constraint is just a set of 4 doubles: a minimum and maximum width, and a minimum and maximum height.") but not in the ledger; claim 1 covers only LayoutBuilder.
issues.quote: during layout, each parent tells its child the smallest and largest width and height it may take
issues.fix: Add to .meta.json claim: "During layout a parent gives each child constraints: minimum and maximum width and height" (kind behavior, version_key flutter, source ui/layout/constraints.md).
